new.name: MeiGen AI Design MCP
new.description: MeiGen AI Design MCP is an MIT-licensed remote MCP server and ChatGPT plugin that lets ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, OpenClaw and other assistants search MeiGen's library of reference images and prompts for inspiration and then generate images and videos with current AI models; searching is free, and generation uses purchased MeiGen credits after an OAuth sign-in.

new.name: vAPI Network
new.description: vapi-network is an Apache-2.0, non-custodial TypeScript client from vAPI Network for finding and paying x402 APIs in USDC on Base from a terminal, an MCP client or your own code; keys stay encrypted on your device, a spend policy is checked before each payment is signed, payments go straight to the provider with no vAPI fee, and each call leaves a local receipt. It is not related to the voice company Vapi.ai.

new.name: avoid-ai-writing
new.description: avoid-ai-writing is an MIT-licensed skill for Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, Hermes and other Agent Skills-compatible agents that finds and removes common AI writing patterns in English text, with a rewrite mode that edits in up to two passes, a detect-only mode that separates real problems from judgment calls, voice profiles and a bundled npm detector.

new.name: peon-ping
new.description: peon-ping is an MIT-licensed notifier that plays game character voice lines, from Warcraft, StarCraft, Portal, Zelda and more, and shows bold on-screen banners when an AI coding agent finishes or needs permission, so you do not lose time after tabbing away; it works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf, OpenCode, Kiro and many others, and includes an MCP server so the agent can pick its own sound.

new.name: bb
new.description: bb is an MIT-licensed agentic IDE that can control, customise and automate itself, which you drive from its desktop app, web app, CLI or HTTP API; work runs in threads you can watch live, steer at any point or hand to another agent. The macOS Apple Silicon app is the main build, with alpha Linux and Windows versions and an npx option.

new.name: obsidian-second-brain
new.description: obsidian-second-brain is an MIT-licensed setup that turns an Obsidian vault of plain Markdown files into persistent memory shared by Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok Bot and other agents, rewriting existing pages as new sources come in rather than just appending; its Crew feature gives several agents one shared logbook of finished jobs in any folder, where a lesson becomes a rule only after a human approves it.

new.name: HAPI
new.description: HAPI is an AGPL-3.0, local-first app that wraps official coding-agent sessions such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent, OpenCode, Copilot and Kimi and lets you control them remotely from native iOS and Android apps, a web app or a Telegram Mini App, so you can approve requests with one tap, run terminal commands from your phone, dictate by voice and switch between desk and phone without restarting the session.

new.name: DevSpace
new.description: DevSpace is an MIT-licensed local layer that lets ChatGPT, Claude, Grok Bot, OpenClaw and Hermes, acting as MCP hosts, open a workspace on your own machine, edit files, run tests and show a diff for review through a tunnel you control, and lets one coding agent hand work to others such as Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor or Copilot as subagents in separate git worktrees, using the CLIs and subscriptions you already have.

stars.name: REA
stars.description: MCP server and CLI that lets coding agents reverse engineer native binaries, Electron and JavaScript apps, .NET assemblies and live websites, using Ghidra, Hopper or IDA under the hood.

stars.name: OpenClaw
stars.description: OpenClaw is an MIT-licensed personal AI assistant that runs on your own computer and answers in the chat apps you already use, including Discord, iMessage, Slack, Teams, Telegram and WhatsApp, with native apps for macOS, iOS, Android, Windows and Linux. State, memory and credentials stay on your hardware, models and harnesses such as Claude, Codex or local models are swappable plugins, and one gateway can run a personal or shared multiplayer assistant. It is stewarded by the non-profit OpenClaw Foundation with no paid tier or hosted service.
stars.pricing_detail: Free and open source (MIT); you pay only for the model providers you connect.

stars.name: ECC
stars.description: The agent harness performance optimization system. Skills, instincts, memory, security, and research-first development for Claude Code, Codex, Opencode, Cursor and beyond

stars.name: DeepSeek Harness
stars.description: DeepSeek's open-source agent harness with a local web UI, built so that every tool, model and scheduled task is a swappable plugin; still a developer preview.

stars.name: Hermes Agent (Nous Research)
stars.description: Hermes Agent is Nous Research's MIT-licensed, self-improving agent with a built-in learning loop: it writes skills from completed tasks, refines them in use, keeps agent-curated memory and searches its own past conversations. It runs on anything from a $5 VPS to serverless infrastructure, offers a full terminal UI, and one gateway serves Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal and the CLI, with any model via Nous Portal, OpenRouter, OpenAI or your own endpoint.
stars.pricing_detail: Free and open source (MIT); model usage billed by your chosen provider.

stars.name: opencode
stars.description: OpenCode is an MIT-licensed open-source AI coding agent for the terminal, with a beta desktop app, that works with many model providers instead of locking you to one. Install it with a one-line script, npm, Homebrew, pacman, mise or Nix, then let it read your repository, edit files and run commands from a keyboard-driven TUI.
stars.pricing_detail: Free and open source (MIT); bring your own model provider.

stars.name: n8n
stars.description: Workflow automation with AI agent nodes; self-host or cloud.

stars.name: Firecrawl
stars.description: Turns websites into clean, LLM-ready data for agents.
